claims.statement: Following 2025 simplification, EUDR applies from 30 December 2026 to large and medium operators and certain timber-regulation SMEs, and from 30 June 2027 to other micro and small operators.
The July 2026 implementation package sets Information System rules and updated APIs, while operators placing covered commodities must demonstrate deforestation-free and legally produced origin.
The hardest mid-market handoff is likely to be correcting supplier polygons and origin documents before shipment, but the frequency and paid value of these exceptions are unmeasured.

contrary_evidence: The revised regime removed much downstream statement work and concentrates responsibility on the first operator, shrinking the originally expected customer set.
The law was delayed and simplified more than once, so buyers may postpone purchasing or expect further change.
Commodity platforms, certification providers, and large importers already have supplier traceability systems.

economics.acquisition_route: Add a commodity-and-CN-code trigger to a freight forwarder's or importer's pre-booking checklist so an in-scope first operator receives an evidence request before cargo departure, not at customs arrival. Use a fixed-fee failed-polygon diagnostic as the entry product and convert recurring shippers to a retainer.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Supplier-language onboarding, reusable legality checklists by origin, robust polygon validation, controlled evidence versioning, API submission, and an exception-resolution queue improve throughput. These operating integrations, not merely accumulated maps, create switching cost.
fingerprint.customer: Medium Polish and CEE operators first placing or exporting covered coffee, cocoa, wood, rubber, soy, palm-oil, or cattle products, especially those with fragmented smallholder or multi-tier suppliers.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Add a commodity-and-CN-code trigger to a freight forwarder's or importer's pre-booking checklist so an in-scope first operator receives an evidence request before cargo departure, not at customs arrival. Use a fixed-fee failed-polygon diagnostic as the entry product and convert recurring shippers to a retainer.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Collect plot polygons and legality records, validate coordinate geometry and harvest dates, screen deforestation risk using official and permitted geospatial layers, chase exceptions in producer languages, and assemble the operator's due-diligence workpaper and Information System payload. The operator retains legal responsibility and final risk judgment.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The operator pays per supplier onboarding and per lot or statement, then a recurring fee for geospatial monitoring and evidence retention; complex coordinate or legality exceptions are separately fixed-priced.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Before a covered lot is purchased, shipped, placed on the market, or exported, the operator lacks valid plot geolocation, legality documents, a risk conclusion, or an Information System submission.

founder_fit: Strong fit with geospatial data, AI-assisted document review, anomaly detection, and FMCG supply-chain understanding.
Asset-light and asynchronous enough for a part-time start if limited to a small number of origin/commodity pairs.
Must avoid any use of confidential employer supply-chain information and obtain specialist legal review of representations.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: EUDR Lot-Evidence and Geospatial Exception Desk
uncertainties: Exception rate by origin and commodity after the 2026 scope update.
Whether freight forwarders will embed pre-booking checks and who bears delay liability.
Extent to which official datasets and supplier evidence support a defensible risk conclusion.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Select one commodity and two origin countries, obtain 20 historical lot packets from three consenting operators, and run a paid defect audit measuring missing, malformed, and overlapping plots plus legality gaps. Continue only if defects are frequent, resolvable before shipment, and at least two operators buy recurring lot processing.
